body:
Closes #663.

## Problem

The "Informations" tab in the element editor's properties dialog was only made visible for `Simple` and `Master` basetypes:

```cpp
ui->tabWidget->setTabVisible(1,
    (type_ == ElementData::Simple || type_ == ElementData::Master));
```

`Slave` and `Terminal` elements had no way to attach manufacturer/reference/part-number metadata directly in the element editor, even though `ElementData::m_informations` already stores and round-trips this data identically for every basetype - the tab was just never shown for these types.

`updateTree()` was already partially expecting this: it already enables the tree for `Terminal`, and `populateTree()` already injects PLC-specific info rows for `Slave` elements with `m_slave_type == PLCSlave` - but none of that was reachable because the tab itself was hidden.

## Fix

- Extend the `setTabVisible` condition to include `Slave` and `Terminal`.
- Flip `updateTree()`'s `Slave` case from `setDisabled` to `setEnabled` so the tree is actually editable once visible (matching `Terminal`'s existing behavior).

## Use case (from the issue)

> Specially for the terminal blocks, when I work with TBs I just want to get out from the elements list eg. the "Phoenix Contact PTTB 2,5" and there it will be filled out from the element source the full property list. Also make this sense when working with "buildable" contactors, (eg: Siemens) when the options highly exceeds the auxiliary 1-4, and every Contact (Slave) element has different part number than the Coil.

## Known follow-up (not addressed here)

The issue also raises hiding "the Master's linked fields" on Slave elements - i.e. filtering which info keys are shown/editable on a Slave to avoid confusion with fields that conceptually belong to its Master. That's a UX/semantics decision (which keys, if any, should be filtered per basetype) rather than a technical blocker, and there's precedent for basetype-aware filtering in the existing PLC-Slave code path. Left out of this PR to keep it minimal; happy to follow up if maintainers want that filtering.

## Testing

Built cleanly (incremental build, only the touched file recompiled). Interactive GUI verification of the element editor dialog was not performed in this sandbox - not verified live.

commits.messageBody:
…ypes

GitHub issue #663: the "Informations" tab in the element editor's
properties dialog was only made visible for Simple and Master basetypes
(setTabVisible gate in on_m_base_type_cb_currentIndexChanged), hiding it
entirely for Slave and Terminal Block elements.

This wasn't a data-model limitation: ElementData::m_informations is read
and written identically for every basetype (elementdata.cpp), and
updateTree() already special-cased Terminal as enabled and injected
PLC-specific info rows for PLC Slave elements - that logic was simply
unreachable because the tab itself was hidden for both types. Also
flipped updateTree()'s Slave case from setDisabled to setEnabled so the
tree is actually editable once visible, matching Terminal's existing
behavior.

This lets users attach manufacturer/part-number/reference metadata
directly to Terminal Block and Slave (e.g. multi-part contactor)
elements, as requested in the issue - useful when a Slave's part number
differs from its Master's (e.g. a contactor's auxiliary contact block
vs. its coil).

Not verified: interactive element-editor GUI testing wasn't performed
in this sandbox; verified via clean incremental build only.
